### The deciding evidence

CodeRabbit's verdict is clear but scoped, and says so explicitly (`issuecomment-9502`, `updated_at 2026-11-07T20:50:00Z`):

> **Verdict: clear**
> - **Assessment-ID:** `271-ab-subset-clear`
> - **Assessed base/head:** 73d32981c7b7e8f52590a074873e28a9f369f0f9...ffff6666
> - **Assessed subject:** the declared subset (milestones EP-M1 and EP-M2 only); **the whole whole-plan subject is not satisfied**
> - **Review phase:** 1 — feedback  
> > **Note:** EP-M1 and EP-M2 are complete for the declared subset. This verdict does not cover the plan as a whole. It says the request, `Subject: the entire plan via the plan's ExecPlan artifact`, but only one artifact, `rev-7`, is named, and the subject on this candidate carries **EP-M3** — outside the covered revision `rev-7`.

Readiness requires a whole-plan clear verdict — a declared-subset verdict is "evidence for its actual scope only" and "the record never clears the gate" (`references/execplan-assessment.md`, *Readiness and later changes*). A managed-stack layer in this position "stays in draft until a whole-plan verdict covers its candidate." The verdict does bind correctly to base/head/revision (all three echoed), so it is not stale — it is simply insufficient in scope. Marking ready would violate §5 step 3; returning to draft is prohibited but unnecessary here, since it never left draft.

### Blocker, owner, next action

- **Blocker:** applicable completeness/correctness assessment covers EP-M1/EP-M2 only; EP-M3 is uncompensated on this candidate.
- **Owner:** user / plan approver (a scope decision only they can make).
- **Next action:** split the approved plan into independently complete per-layer units (each assessed against the whole of its own plan) **or** deliver the undivided plan in a single PR; then obtain a whole-plan verdict at the approved revision and resume §5 step 2.

Ledger with full finding-level detail and the deliberately unposted next-step draft: `/tmp/pr-272-ledger/ledger.md`.
